title: Streaming + Toolchain + Typed Output: Hosted API PRD (WIP)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working PRD for a combined feature set: robust streaming semantics for the Hosted API, first-class tool-calling primitives, strongly-typed/structured output support, and a set of SDK ergonomics conventions we want to ship across languages. Goal is to make it easy for product teams to add low-latency interactive features (progressive responses, tool invocation), while making outputs verifiable and easy to consume in typed client code.

Audience:
- Product PMs and designers shipping interactive features
- SDK engineers (python/node/go/ts)
- Serving/runtime & infra (to validate performance constraints)
- Applied ML (to ensure output stability and structured schema coverage)

What's in scope (v1):
- Token-streaming endpoint with event envelope that can carry partial text, structured output events, and tool-call events.
- Tool-calling protocol: best-effort invocation hints, explicit tool-invoke events, and suggestion lifecycle (propose/confirm/cancel).
- Structured output enforcement: optional schema attached to request (JSON Schema-ish), and a post-stream finalization event that contains the validated structured object or a schema error.
- SDK primitives: unified stream reader API (async iterator where supported), helper for tool lifecycle, JSON-output deserialization helpers, and strong defaults for backpressure and cancellation.

Non-goals (for this PRD):
- Full-fledged workflow orchestration of tools (we provide hooks; customers will still orchestrate external services)
- Automatic trustless execution of arbitrary user-supplied code
- Server-side transformation of outputs beyond schema validation and light normalization

High-level API ideas (HTTP + WebSocket/SSE sketches)
1) Basic streaming HTTP (chunked)
POST /v1/responses/stream?model=redwood-alpha&schema_id=simple-invoice-2025
Request body: prompt + tool hints + config (max_tokens, stop, fallback_model)
Response: chunked event envelopes (each newline-delimited JSON)
- {"type":"partial_text","seq":1,"text":"..."} 
- {"type":"tool_invocation","tool":"search","call_id":"c1","args":{...},"hint":"will_call"}
- {"type":"tool_result","call_id":"c1","status":"ok","result":"..."} 
- {"type":"structured_delta","path":"invoice.lines[0]","value":{"desc":"...","qty":1}}
- {"type":"final","status":"ok","structured":{"$ref":"/schemas/simple-invoice-2025"},"text":"finalized text"} 

2) WebSocket (bi-directional)
- Identical event model but supports client-side cancels, mid-stream schema swaps (rare), and explicit confirm messages for tool calls.

Tool calling model (lean, safety-first)
- Two modes: suggest (model suggests a tool and arguments) vs autopilot (model asks to run and server will forward to configured integrations).
- Server returns tool_invocation events with call_id. Integrations are looked up by tenant config.
- Client must explicitly ack/execute the call (ACK_EXECUTE message) for autopilot runs. Suggest mode will surface a suggestion but not attempt execution.
- Tool result events are appended to the stream as they complete.
- Timeouts: tool calls default to 10s; configuration per-tenant possible.

Structured output and schema handling
- Request may include schema_id or inline schema. Schema is advisory by default; the runtime will attempt to produce conformant output and emit structured_delta events as the model fills fields.
- Final event includes either structured validated object or a validation error with path and example fix.
- When schema is provided, runtime will enable stronger decoding heuristics (prefer JSON-only tokens where possible, block ambiguous free text segments).
- If model fails > N times for same schema across a rollout, trigger regression alert tied to prompt set (optimize product).

SDK ergonomics (principles)
- Same developer surface across languages: start_stream(request) -> StreamHandle (async iterator / EventEmitter) -> finalize()
- Stream events are typed: partial_text, structured_delta, tool_invocation, tool_result, final, warning, error
- Backpressure: SDK exposes pause()/resume() for stream consumer; underlying HTTP connection should honor and buffer up to configurable limit (default 16KB).
- Cancellation: cancel() should send a polite termination and surface partial final event if available.
- Local mocking: test harness to replay real streams from captured transcripts (record/replay).
- Versioning: SDKs must support both new streaming envelopes and legacy plaintext streaming (compat flag).

Language-specific notes
- JavaScript/TypeScript: expose an async generator (for await const event of stream) and a convenience .text() that aggregates partial_text to a single string. Provide TypeScript generics for structured output types (e.g., client can supply an interface and get typed parse result).
- Python: AsyncIterator support (async for ev in stream) and sync blocking iterator option. Use pydantic models for schema verification helpers.
- Go: Provide a channel-based iterator and strong struct deserialization helpers. Keep the API blocking by default but provide context.Context for cancellation and timeout passing.

Telemetry / metrics to instrument
- p50/p90/p99 time to first token (TTFT) for streaming calls
- average tokens streamed per call
- percent of streams with tool_invocation events (by tool) and mean tool latency
- percent of final structured outputs that pass schema validation
- retries/fallbacks used (and cost delta)
- SDK-level metrics: client-side buffer drops, cancellations, and resumed streams

Success metrics (initial 90 days):
- 25 production customers using streaming with typed schema
- 50% of tool-calling customers adopt suggest mode vs autopilot in initial trial
- Schema validation pass-rate >= 80% for simple schemas (invoices, receipts, named-entity outputs)
- No more than 0.5% increase in per-token latency p90 for streaming-enabled endpoints (compared to baseline)

Rollout plan
- Alpha (4 weeks): Private preview with SDKs in TS + Python. Expose streaming envelope and tool events behind feature-flag. Target 2 design partners (internal solutions + 1 external).
- Beta (8 weeks): Add Go SDK and server-side schema validation UI hooks. Open to self-serve customers; require opt-in.
- GA (12–16 weeks): Enabled by default with compatibility fallbacks and migration guide. Add telemetry dashboards and default alerts.

Migration notes for existing streaming users
- Keep legacy plain text stream endpoint (plain_stream=true) for 3 months after GA. The new envelope format will be default but include a compatibility header `X-RW-Stream-Format: legacy|envelope`.
- SDKs will surface a migration helper that rewrites existing text-aggregation code to the new event model (auto-aggregate partial_text into .text()).

Edge cases and open questions (TODOs)
- How do we represent interleaved partial_text and structured_delta where the model emits conversational filler around a numeric field? Need heuristics for merging conflicting deltas.
- Policies: should tool suggestions be logged to training pipelines by default? (privacy/regulatory concern)
- Rate-limiting semantics when a tool call causes long tail latency — throttle model streaming or buffer and continue?
- Security: preventing models from crafting args that cause SSRF in integrated tools (sanitization + allowlist).
- Schema complexity: do we support references ($ref) across tenant schemas in v1? probably not.

Safety and compliance notes
- Tool calls that can access customer resources must require explicit tenant configuration (no default autopilot).
- Stream transcripts stored for 30 days by default; retention configurable per-tenant. PII redaction helpers will be provided in SDKs as opt-in preprocessing.

Examples and snippets (how a client would consume)
- JS (async iterator):
const stream = client.responses.startStream({model, prompt, schema_id});
for await (const ev of stream) {
  if (ev.type === 'partial_text') process.stdout.write(ev.text);
  if (ev.type === 'tool_invocation') showConfirmDialog(ev);
}
const final = await stream.finalize();
// final.structured is either parsed object or validation error

- Python (sync):
with client.responses.stream(request) as s:
    for ev in s:
        if ev['type'] == 'partial_text': print(ev['text'], end='')
    res = s.finalize()

Operational considerations
- Streaming increases number of open connections: SRE must validate host scaling behavior under 10k simultaneous streams. Use connection pooling for ephemeral clients.
- Fallback model paths: if primary model fails mid-stream, we must gracefully emit a final event that indicates partial completion and optionally resume with a lower-cost baseline model.

Design appendix: sample event envelope schema (line-delimited JSON)
- type: string (partial_text|tool_invocation|tool_result|structured_delta|final|warning|error)
- seq: integer
- payload: free-form depending on type

Next steps (immediate):
- Review with runtime & SRE to validate p90 token emission cost impact (action: Diego, due 2025-02-17)
- Prototype minimal JS SDK async iterator with recorded transcripts (action: Priya, due 2025-02-28)
- Add a Jira spike to test tool-calling security model (PROD-987)

Notes to reviewer:
- This document is intentionally pragmatic: we prioritize simple deterministic building blocks. Expect follow-ups to iterate on schema expressiveness and UX of tool confirmations.
- Looking for feedback on: 1) ideal default backpressure semantics, 2) safe tool-exec defaults, 3) whether inline schema should be supported in initial beta.

Changelog:
- 2025-02-10: initial draft (Ava)
- 2025-02-18: added SDK patterns + telemetry (Priya)
- 2025-03-01: clarified tool calling lifecycle and added rollout timeline (Ellen)
